# `git merge --abort` after a sesam merge: git restores the objects, but the
# gitignored revealed file is left as the driver's merged output until re-revealed.
# `sesam open` recovers ours' content and the repo verifies. (No auto re-reveal on
# abort - see A8.)

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp ours.txt $TMPDIR/ours.txt
cp theirs.txt $TMPDIR/theirs.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt secret.txt
exec sesam add secret.txt --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

exec git checkout -b ours
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt secret.txt
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: first line'

exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt secret.txt
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: last line'

exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs

# Abort: the pending merge is gone.
exec git merge --abort
! exec git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD

# Re-reveal recovers ours' content and the repo verifies.
exec sesam open
grep 'first = OURS' secret.txt
grep 'last = BASE' secret.txt
! grep 'THEIRS' secret.txt
exec sesam verify

-- base.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = BASE

-- ours.txt --
first = OURS
middle = BASE
last = BASE

-- theirs.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = THEIRS
